title: Craft a Story with a Beginning and an End
subtitle: Learn to choose and develop story ideas.
objectives: Identify the three key parts of a story: beginning, problem, and ending.
Use a digital tool to brainstorm story possibilities.
Rewrite a story's ending to solve the problem creatively.

scenes.title: Great Stories
scenes.narration: What makes a story great? It's how events connect. Every good story has a clear start, a challenge, and a satisfying finish. Let's build one!
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon character holds up a book, then three distinct panels slide in: 'Beginning', 'Problem', 'Ending'.

scenes.title: Story Structure
scenes.narration: The beginning introduces characters and setting. A problem arises, the main challenge. The ending shows its solution. These three parts are the story's backbone.
scenes.visualAction: The character points to each panel as its name is narrated. A question mark appears over 'Problem', then a checkmark over 'Ending'.

scenes.title: Kite's Adventure
scenes.narration: Imagine a kite soaring high, needing a safe place to land as evening approaches. That's our beginning and problem. We will explore two ending options.
scenes.visualAction: A cartoon kite flies across the screen. The sun starts to set. A friendly character appears, pointing to a grassy field. The kite gently descends.

scenes.title: Connected Endings
scenes.narration: A strong ending always connects to the problem. If the kite needs to land safely, the ending must show it landing safely. It resolves the main challenge.
scenes.visualAction: The kite lands softly in the field. The character gives a thumbs up. A thought bubble appears with a question mark, then a checkmark over the landed kite.

scenes.title: Making it Better
scenes.narration: Digital tools offer ideas, but they can be too simple. You can take a basic idea and make it unique. Add your creative touch to make the story truly yours.
scenes.visualAction: A generic 'AI' icon appears, then a thought bubble with a simple ending. The character shakes their head, then smiles as they write on a notepad, showing a more detailed ending.

scenes.title: Your Turn to Create
scenes.narration: Now it's your turn! We have a kite story beginning and problem, plus two endings. Choose one ending and rewrite it. Solve the kite's problem clearly!
scenes.visualAction: The character presents two thought bubbles with different ending options. A pencil icon appears, inviting the learner to write.

scenes.title: Mission Complete!
scenes.narration: Fantastic work! You've learned to build a story with a clear beginning, problem, and connected ending. Your creativity makes a story special. Keep practicing!
scenes.visualAction: The character claps. The kite flies happily. A trophy icon appears, then a speech bubble saying 'Great Story!'

reading.title: Story Structure
reading.text: Every good story has three main parts: a beginning, a problem, and an ending. The beginning introduces characters and setting. The problem is the challenge they face. The ending shows how the problem is solved or what happens next.

reading.title: The Kite's Journey
reading.text: Our story begins with a paper kite flying high, but evening is near, and it needs a safe landing spot (the problem). A friendly character helps it find a grassy field. The ending must show the kite landing safely, solving its problem.

reading.title: Your Creative Choice
reading.text: Digital tools can offer ideas, but your unique touch makes a story great. Always check if the ending truly solves the problem. Don't just accept the first idea; choose and rewrite to make it better and more connected.

materials.title: Invented kite story
materials.text: An imaginary kite needs somewhere to land before evening. Option 1: a friendly bird points out an empty grassy space. Option 2: an imaginary friend draws a map to an empty grassy space. Choose an idea and write your own two-sentence ending.

promptExamples.initial: Write a story about a kite.
promptExamples.improved: Write a story about a paper kite that needs to land safely before dark. Include a beginning, a problem, and an ending where it finds a safe spot.
promptExamples.followup: The ending you provided doesn't quite solve the kite's problem of needing a safe landing. Can you rewrite it so the kite finds a secure place on the ground?

activity.title: Rewrite the Ending
activity.instructions: Choose one of the two ideas and rewrite it in exactly two sentences of your own. Your ending should resolve the landing problem.
activity.starter: An imaginary kite needs somewhere to land before evening. Option 1: a friendly bird points out an empty grassy space. Option 2: an imaginary friend draws a map to an empty grassy space. Choose an idea and write your own two-sentence ending.
activity.expectedEvidence: Two original sentences with an ending connected to the problem.

quiz.question: Which option is outside the three-part story structure taught in this lesson: beginning, problem and ending?
quiz.explanation: The title introduces the story, but it's not one of the three main structural parts (beginning, problem, ending) that make up the narrative flow. The beginning sets the scene, the problem introduces the conflict, and the ending provides the resolution.

quiz.question: In the kite story, what was the main problem?
options: The kite was too high in the sky.
The kite needed a safe place to land before dark.
The kite was a bright red color.
quiz.explanation: The story explicitly states the kite 'needed a safe place to land before dark' as evening approached. Its height is part of the setting, and its color is a descriptive detail, not the central conflict.

quiz.question: In an invented story, a travelling library cannot deliver its books because the book box is locked. The librarian has its key. Which ending resolves that problem?
options: The library van gets a new colour.
The librarian unlocks the box with the key and delivers the books.
quiz.explanation: Unlocking the box and delivering the books resolve the stated problem. The other endings leave it unresolved.

mission.title: The Traveling Library Story
mission.instructions: Write a 3–5 sentence story about an imaginary travelling library. Introduce the library, give it a specific problem, and write an ending connected to that problem. Explain one creative choice you made yourself.
rubric: The story has a clear beginning that introduces the traveling library.
A specific problem is introduced that the library faces.
The ending clearly solves the problem presented.
The story is 3-5 sentences long and easy to understand.

hints.question: What should I include in the beginning of my story?
hints.answer: In the beginning, introduce your traveling library bus and where it's going. For example, 'The bright blue traveling library bus set off for the quiet village of Willow Creek.'

hints.question: How can I make sure my ending solves the problem?
hints.answer: Think about the problem you created. If the problem was a flat tire, the ending should describe how the tire was fixed or replaced so the bus could continue its journey. The solution should directly address the challenge.

hints.question: Can you give me an idea for a problem?
hints.answer: A good problem for the traveling library could be a sudden heavy rainstorm making the road muddy and impassable, or a bridge being out, blocking the path to a village.

imageBrief.title: The Traveling Library
imageBrief.scenario: A traveling library bus faces a problem on its journey to a remote village, and then finds a solution.
imageBrief.composition: Three distinct panels, arranged horizontally. Panel 1: A cheerful, colorful library bus on a sunny road. Panel 2: The bus stuck in mud or facing a broken bridge, with a worried driver. Panel 3: The bus successfully arriving at a small, happy village, with children eagerly waiting.
imageBrief.altText: A three-panel comic showing a traveling library bus. First, it's driving happily. Second, it's stuck or blocked. Third, it has arrived and children are reading books.

educatorNotes.sampleAnswer: Activity: a friendly imaginary bird shows the kite an empty grassy space. The kite lands before evening and is pleased with its new resting place. Mission: a travelling library arrives with a locked book box; the librarian unlocks it with the key; the readers receive their books. Accept different connected endings and the learner's explanation of a creative choice.
educatorNotes.commonMisconception: A common misconception is that any event after the problem counts as an ending, even if it doesn't resolve the initial conflict. Students might introduce a new problem or a disconnected event instead of a solution.
reviewChecks: The story has a clear beginning that introduces the traveling library.
A specific problem is introduced that the library faces.
The ending clearly solves the problem presented.
The story is 3-5 sentences long and easy to understand.
educatorNotes.safetyNotes: When discussing the kite story, remind students that flying kites near power lines or busy roads is dangerous. Always have an adult present when flying kites outdoors.
